neighbours.label: a verb of making something new (' developed', ' created', ' engineered', ' built') describing what researchers did, as opposed to finding or measuring
fire: Scientists at the university have developed a cheap sensor that detects lead in tap water.
A team in Zurich has engineered bacteria that glow when exposed to arsenic.
Researchers have created a new battery material that charges in under five minutes.
Chemists in Kyoto designed a molecule that breaks down plastic waste at room temperature.
The group built a tiny robot that can swim through blood vessels.
Engineers have invented a coating that keeps ice from forming on aircraft wings.
Physicists at the lab have fabricated a laser smaller than a grain of sand.
Researchers in Boston have developed a test that spots the virus in ten minutes.
quiet: Scientists at the university have found high levels of lead in tap water across the city.
A team in Zurich has observed bacteria that glow when exposed to arsenic.
Researchers have measured how quickly a common battery material loses its charge.
Chemists in Kyoto noticed that plastic waste breaks down slowly at room temperature.
The group studied a tiny fish that can swim through narrow underwater caves.
Engineers have reported that ice often forms on aircraft wings in winter.
Physicists at the lab have detected a faint signal from a distant star.
Researchers in Boston have confirmed that the virus spreads mostly indoors.

notes: Card: ' developed' x7, ' engineered', ' create', ' build', ' strategy' in science-news 'researchers have ___'. The - pole is completion/removal participles ('completed', 'eliminated', 'removed'). Near misses keep 'researchers have' but use discovery/measurement verbs, testing creation vs observation.
